findings.description: publicly_accessible = true gives the RDS instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, dramatically expanding the attack surface of the MySQL service and enabling direct credential brute-force. This is aggravated by skip_final_snapshot = true and no deletion protection. Severity high, not critical, because ingress is constrained to the VPC CIDR (see aws_security_group_rule.catalog_db_inbound) rather than 0.0.0.0/0.

storage_encrypted = false leaves the database storage, automated snapshots, and any read replicas unencrypted, exposing stored application data to anyone with access to the underlying volumes or a snapshot copy.

The RDS master password (var.password) is interpolated in cleartext into the EC2 user_data script and written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc, and the master username is the static, guessable value "admin". The IAM instance profile also grants rds:* account-wide (see aws_iam_role_policy.catalog_app_policy), so this credential is usable to take over database infrastructure.

The user_data script embeds the DB server, username, and master password in a PHP include file under the web root, and the surrounding heredocs are passed verbatim to the app instance, leaking live database credentials to anyone able to read user_data (EC2 metadata service) or the served file.

The policy attached to the EC2-assumable catalog role allows s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", granting account-wide control of object storage, compute, and databases. An attacker who compromises the catalog app server inherits this role and can exfiltrate or destroy data and pivot throughout the account.

MySQL port 3306 is opened to the whole VPC CIDR rather than only the application security group, so every host in the VPC — including any compromised or unrelated workload — can reach the database directly, bypassing network segmentation.

The database security group permits all outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 on every protocol, so a compromised database can exfiltrate data and establish callbacks to attacker-controlled infrastructure without restriction.

The RDS instance, its subnet group, and the parameter group enforce no TLS requirement (no require_secure_transport / rds.force_ssl=1), and the application connects with plain mysqli_connect without SSL options; credentials and query data therefore travel in cleartext between the app tier and the database.
The MySQL 8.0 parameter group only sets character-set parameters and never enables require_secure_transport, so the database will accept unencrypted client connections over its network endpoint.
